details: company headquartered in McLean, Virginia that specializes in artificial intelligence and machine learning for human language technologies. The company provides both managed and professional services for natural language processing (NLP) technologies including automatic speech recognition (ASR), neural machine translation (MT), natural-language understanding (NLU) and neural speech synthesis. AppTek's Head of Science, Prof. Dr. -Ing Hermann Ney, was awarded the IEEE James L. Flanagan Speech and Audio Processing Award in 2019 and the ISCA Medal for Scientific Achievement in 2021 for his work in natural language processing.

explainer.lead: AppTek is a U.S. company that builds and provides services for technologies that work with human language, including speech recognition and machine translation. Its work matters because it connects several language capabilities, from turning speech into text to understanding, translating, and synthesizing language.

tiers.eli5: AppTek makes computer tools that help people work with spoken and written language. Think of a helpful language assistant that can listen to speech, write down what was said, translate it into another language, and read the result aloud. The company also provides services to help organizations use these tools.
tiers.practitioner: AppTek can be used as a provider of managed or professional services for ASR, neural machine translation, natural-language understanding, and neural speech synthesis. An application might pass recorded speech through recognition and translation before generating synthesized speech. The company rebuilt its machine-translation platform with neural approaches after selling its hybrid machine-translation technology to eBay in 2014.
tiers.paperLevel: AppTek is an organization applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to human language technologies, rather than a single algorithm or model. Its named technical areas are automatic speech recognition, neural machine translation, natural-language understanding, and neural speech synthesis. No specific model architectures, training datasets, or benchmark results are given.

explainer.example: A recorded sentence in one language can be transcribed by automatic speech recognition, translated into another language by neural machine translation, and then read aloud through neural speech synthesis.

usedIn.name: Neural machine translation
